scope: Targeted inspection of two primary full-text papers for conditional odds e-variables, continuous prior mixtures, Jeffreys terminology, and the local signed/common-order argument. No simulator calls, new Monte Carlo, prospective files, or trial ledgers were used.

primary_papers.title: Generic E-Variables for Exact Sequential k-Sample Tests that allow for Optional Stopping
primary_papers.access: Primary full HTML inspected and cached locally.

locators.label: Section 7.2: The Conditional E-variable for Tests of Two Proportions
locators.finding: For size-2 blocks with one observation per side, the paper conditions on the pair total and defines the conditional odds likelihood ratio q_delta(Y_a,Y_b | Y_a+Y_b)/q_0(Y_a,Y_b | Y_a+Y_b). The conditional null law is nuisance-independent, giving an e-variable. Concordant pairs have factor one. The discussion attributes the construction to Wald (1947).

locators.label: Section 1.1, Definition 1 and equations (1.2)-(1.4)
locators.finding: Conditional e-variable products, likelihood-ratio test martingales, and the Ville threshold 1/alpha are explicit background.

locators.label: Section 2.1, Theorem 1 and equations (2.2)-(2.3)
locators.finding: The paper also constructs generic full-data two-stream e-variables. Section 7.2 identifies its generic Bernoulli factor as growth-rate optimal in the specified model and compares the pair-conditional factor unfavorably in growth.

limits: The directly inspected conditional two-proportion construction in Section 7.2 is m=1. This review does not attribute our exact larger balanced-block continuous mixture, signed changing-probability common-order argument, or certified quadrature algorithm to that section.
The authors refer to experimental growth comparisons not reported there; this is not an independently reproduced sample-cost benchmark for FaultTune.
Appendix S2 excluding a fixed-success hypergeometric sampling scheme from a Bayes-factor discussion does not negate the explicit random-total conditional e-variable of Section 7.2.
Wald (1947) is a historical attribution in this inspected paper, not an independently inspected third primary source.

primary_papers.title: Safe Testing
primary_papers.access: Primary full HTML inspected and cached locally.

locators.label: Section 1.3, Definition 1, Proposition 2, Corollary 1 and equation (7)
locators.finding: Conditional e-variables may be selected from available past information if conditional safety holds. Products form test supermartingales; the Ville-Robbins boundary is 1/alpha.

locators.label: Example 1 and equation (8)
locators.finding: For a simple null and arbitrary prior W on alternatives, prior-mixture likelihood ratios provide e-variables. Posterior-predictive updates telescope to the original prior marginal likelihood.

locators.label: Example 5: Exponential Families with a point null: Jeffreys Prior
locators.finding: For a regular d-dimensional exponential family, a point null, and a compact interior parameter restriction, the paper discusses Jeffreys priors and (d/2) log n + O(1) regret, attributed to Clarke and Barron (1994).

limits: The model-dependent Jeffreys prior in Example 5 must not be equated automatically to Beta(1/2,1/2) on q=logistic(lambda) for a general conditional hypergeometric block design.
The regular, asymptotic, compact-interior regret discussion does not establish the exact local finite-sample Lipschitz bound or its validity at adaptive or boundary parameters.
Generic optional continuation alone does not prove the local signed common-order decision rule. Its explicit domination proof is still needed.
Clarke and Barron (1994) is cited background; its original paper was not independently inspected in this targeted review.

claim_crosswalk.claim: Conditioning out the common Bernoulli success probability and accumulating sequential odds evidence
claim_crosswalk.evidence: Turner, Ly and Grunwald, Section 7.2, especially the m=1 pair-conditional factor.

claim_crosswalk.claim: Fixed continuous prior mixing and inverse-risk stopping boundaries
claim_crosswalk.evidence: Safe Testing, Section 1.3 and Example 1; Turner, Ly and Grunwald, Section 1.1.

claim_crosswalk.claim: The chosen density rho(lambda)=1/(2*pi*cosh(lambda/2)) is Jeffreys
claim_crosswalk.evidence: It is the change of variables of the Bernoulli-q Beta(1/2,1/2) prior, as established locally. No claim that it is the Jeffreys prior of every conditional hypergeometric design is supported.

claim_crosswalk.claim: A single threshold 1/delta controls directional error under a common order with changing probabilities and predictable balanced blocks
claim_crosswalk.evidence: The local proof uses 1/2 plus the opposite-sign half mixture to dominate the signed error event. The two inspected papers do not by themselves establish that exact extension.

claim_crosswalk.claim: Data-adaptive rational-odds quadrature gives a certified lower bound on one fixed continuous mixture
claim_crosswalk.evidence: The local concavity and outward-rounding construction is supported by the separately bound independent mathematical and numerical review. This search did not establish novelty.

claim_crosswalk.claim: The explicit finite-sample comparison M >= L(lambda*)/[pi*(n+1/2)*cosh(lambda*/2)]
claim_crosswalk.evidence: This is the local Lipschitz integration bound. General logarithmic mixture-regret results are prior art; no claim that this is the first such bound is justified.

claim_crosswalk.claim: The continuous construction has exceeded state of the art in stopping cost
claim_crosswalk.evidence: Literature inspection and deterministic mathematical checks are not stopping-cost benchmarks. A terminal-checkpoint replay is also not a first-crossing comparison.

conclusion: The conditional-odds and safe-mixture framework has direct antecedents. The current result is a mathematically reviewed and numerically certified local construction with unresolved priority, not a newly established statistical framework or a demonstrated full-field SOTA result.
next_comparison_requirements: Retain the frozen prospective study unchanged; continuous Fisher belongs to a subsequent explicitly frozen candidate study.

Map applicable full-data growth-rate-optimal or predictive safe two-sample factors into the comparator inventory, verifying equal information access, common-order assumptions, risk level and physical-shot accounting before treating them as direct competitors.

Use new first-crossing measurements and prespecified risk/error and cost summaries to decide whether continuous integration actually improves stopping cost; a selected terminal-evidence replay only motivates that experiment.
Broader literature coverage is required before making priority or international-leading claims.
